**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Current handling of readiness/startupProbe result updates don't include an immediate sync after declaring the container as failed.
Thus, the sync is done via slower async methods.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Faster update the pod status reacting on probe results. Among other changes, the first readiness probe will be called faster when startup probes succeeded, which will make Pod status as ready faster.

> Having previously dug through this code and its multitude of code paths, I'm a little worried about accidental/unintentional behaviour changes from this refactor...

The code is the same... I still call `SetContainerReadiness` and `SetContainerStartup` only now I call explicitly for a pod sync to ensure we don't have to wait for the periodic reconciliation.
As you can see, it dramatically speeds up pod status updates after probe results, solving a lot of issues.
It's true, however, some things could break if some users were counting on this slowness in their workflows.

review_comments: Can you explain why it is advantageous to handle these all this way in this sync loop? Why were readinessManager and startupManager not in here before? Would it make sense to have the livenessManager behave like them rather than the other way around? (I wish this was documented in a comment from before!)
The main benefit, apart from being easier to present/understand, is to allow me to call the `HandlePodSyncs` in a consistent manner after each *Manager update.
should the `manualTriggerCh` be closed here? What's the risk of keeping it not closed ever?
well, we could say the same for the `stopCh` no?
yes. Not sure what the downside will be to not close it.
I leave it like that, let's see what the approvers have to say.
add logging that we failed to manually trigger the update?
I don't know... does it work putting a log under `default`?
